paper.title: Random Hypervolume Scalarizations for Provable Multi-Objective Black Box Optimization

settings.name_in_paper: Multi-objective Bayesian optimization with GP priors (hypervolume regret)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Multi-objective (vector-valued) rewards; regret measured via hypervolume of the Pareto frontier.
unmapped: k objectives, each an independent GP sample f_i ~ GP(0, kappa_i); noisy vector observation F(x)+noise
regret is hypervolume regret HV_z(Y*) - HV_z(Y_t) w.r.t. reference point z
settings.definition_quote: For multi-objective Bayesian optimization, we assume that all objectives $f_i$ are samples from known GP priors $\GP(0, \kappa_i)$ with input domain $\X$.

settings.name_in_paper: Multi-objective black-box optimization via any single-objective optimizer
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Multi-objective (vector-valued) optimization with hypervolume error objective.
unmapped: guarantee is relative to an arbitrary single-objective optimizer with convergence epsilon_T
settings.definition_quote: Let $F(\X) \subseteq [0, B]^{k}$ and $z \geq 0$ and let $\alg$ be any single-objective maximization algorithm on objective function $g(x)$ that guarantees that after $T$ iterations, it returns $x_T$ such that $g(x_T) \geq g(x^*) - \epsilon_T$

algorithms.name: Algorithm 1 (random hypervolume scalarization with UCB or TS acquisition)

conditions: each f_i on [0,1]^n is a GP sample with marginal variance <= 1
gamma_T upper bounds the MIG of every objective
tuning: D_lambda uniform on positive unit sphere S_+^{k-1}

source.label: thm:hyper_regret
source.quote: Assume the conditions in Theorem~\ref{thm:regret} holds and let $F(\X) \subseteq [0, 2/5]^{k}$ and $z \geq 0$ and $Y_t = F(X_t)$. Running Algorithm~\ref{alg:scalarization} with hypervolume scalarizations ... produces hypervolume regret after $T$ observations that is bounded by: $$\sum_{t=1}^T (\HV_z(Y^* ) - \HV_z(Y_t)) \leq O(k^2 n^{1/2} [ \gamma_T T\ln(T)]^{1/2})$$

results.notes: Cumulative hypervolume regret; derived from the expected (over lambda and GP prior) cumulative scalarized regret of Paria et al., so effectively a Bayesian expectation. Paper's n is input dimension d.

conditions: each f_i on [0,1]^n is a GP sample with marginal variance <= 1
results.notes: Final hypervolume gap after T observations (monotonicity argument). Not a cumulative quantity.

bound.regime: after l*T observations with l = O~((2B)^{k^2} k^{k+1}/(c_k^{k-1} eps_T^{k+1}))

symbols.eps_T: convergence guarantee of the single-objective algorithm after T iterations
symbols.B_range: objective range bound, F(X) subset of [0,B]^k

conditions: single-objective algorithm guarantees g(x_T) >= g(x*) - eps_T after T iterations

source.label: thm:hyper_regret_general
source.quote: Then, running Algorithm~\ref{alg:scalarization_general} on hypervolume scalarizations with reference point $z$ and $D_\lambda = \Sphere^{k-1}$ with $l = \widetilde{O}((2B)^{k^2} k^{k+1}/(c_k^{k-1}\epsilon_T^{k+1}))$ converges to the Pareto frontier and after $l\cdot T$ observations, we have $$\HV_z(Y_T) \geq \HV_z(Y^*) - 5 c_k \epsilon_T$$

results.notes: Theorem statement does not state a probability; proof uses concentration with probability 1-delta (log(1/delta) hidden in O~). Hypervolume error bound.
